core.title: Commons domain modules import nothing outward
core.given: A production source module assigned the domain role within the shared (commons) code tree — the intersection of the domain role location and the shared code tree placement
core.when: it has an import (new or pre-existing) whose resolved target lies in the application or integration role
core.then: Remove the outward import: the domain in the shared code tree MUST NOT import application or integration code; dependencies point inward only.
prefer: Move genuinely domain-owned data or behavior into domain.
Invert an outer capability behind a domain-facing port.

During GREEN: prefer existing domain types, functions, and ports; introduce a new port only when the current behavior requires the domain to request an outer capability, and keep it as narrow as the acceptance requires.
avoid: Importing outward as a temporary shortcut.
Moving unrelated application or integration behavior into domain.
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Imports that resolve outside the project graph (recognised per the profile's external-import idiom) are not layer-checked.
A file that no role is assigned to (per the profile's role assignment) is outside the rule, not in violation.
core.why: The domain is the centre holding the rules and must not know what orchestrates or transports them; an outward import makes the rules unusable without the machinery, first seen as a domain test needing a database.
evidence: The domain in the shared code tree imports no application or integration code: the stack's import-graph check reports no import from such a module resolving into the application or integration role.
verification: Check scope: production source modules at the intersection of the shared code tree placement and the domain role location (profile: layout.commons_dir composed with roles.domain.path; the composed concrete trees are the profile values, not core text); files to which no role is assigned are out of scope, not violations.
An outbound import is an import whose resolved target lies in the application or integration role; the check applies to existing as well as newly changed imports.
Test files are never scanned; the exact vendored and generated trees that are never scanned are the stack's single excluded-trees list (roots.excluded), as classified by the checker.
Imports that resolve outside the project graph are not layer-checked; the profile states how such imports are recognised.
The check does not cover the inward direction: an application or integration module importing domain code does not fire this rule.
A finding from the stack's import-graph / clean-architecture detector is an optional signal or evidence, not a prerequisite.

facts.note: The module is assigned the domain role and lies in the shared code tree; the subject scope is the intersection of the domain role location and the shared tree placement (profile: role assignment, roles.domain.path, layout.commons_dir); files with no assigned role are outside the rule.
Only production source is scanned; test files and vendored/build trees are never scanned.

Import-graph observer: any import (existing or newly changed) in such a domain module whose resolved target lies in the application or integration role; imports resolving outside the project graph are excluded. Role/file-kind facts alone cannot resolve import targets. A detector finding is an optional signal/evidence, not a prerequisite.

fires: A domain module in the shared code tree has an import (new or pre-existing) resolving into the application role.
A domain module in the shared code tree imports a helper from the integration role (e.g. a persistence or transport adapter).
A domain module in the shared code tree imports an outer-layer type as a temporary shortcut to make a test pass.
doesNotFire: A test file under the domain tree imports application code (tests are not scanned).
A file in a vendored or build directory.
A domain module imports an external package specifier (outside the project graph).
A file whose path assigns it no role.
An application or integration module importing from domain (inward direction).

profileRequirements.meaning: Where files of the domain role live stack-wide, independent of this rule's shared-tree scope; combined with the shared code tree placement (layout.commons_dir) its intersection is this rule's subject scope.
Placement of the shared (commons) code tree; this rule's subject scope is the intersection of this placement and the domain role location (roles.domain.path).
profileRequirements.bunValue: the `commons/` and `shared/` trees — composed with the `domain` layer segment this yields the subject globs **/commons/domain/** and **/shared/domain/**

profileRequirements.meaning: Where files of the application role live; an import from a scoped domain module resolving here is an outbound import.
Where files of the integration role live; an import from a scoped domain module resolving here is an outbound import.
How a file is assigned to a role, and that a file with no assigned role is out of scope rather than in violation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the path's layer segment; files with no layer segment are outside the rule, not in violation

profileRequirements.meaning: How an import that resolves outside the project graph is recognised; such imports are not layer-checked.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully stack-neutral; only its anchors are realization data, and no core text names a stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path. (1) The subject scope is expressed as an intersection of two independent profile keys — layout.commons_dir (the shared/commons tree placement) and roles.domain.path (the stack-wide domain role location) — which, instantiated with the Bun values (commons/ and shared/ trees x the `domain` layer segment), compose to the exact Bun subject globs **/commons/domain/** and **/shared/domain/**; that composition is recorded only in profileRequirements.bunValue, never in core text, so roles.domain.path is not overloaded with this rule's scope. The application/integration target locations (roles.application.path, roles.integration.path), the layer-segment role assignment (roles.assignment), and the bare-specifier external-import idiom (idiom.external_import) are likewise profile data, so another stack names its trees and imports differently without changing the core. (2) The only genuinely Bun-only content is the detector/validator id bun_clean_architecture_detector (evidence[1], activation.facts[3] note) and the term ids commons_domain / outbound_import, which stay in the Bun realization; core:verification describes the check generically. (3) Severity 3 and the strict disposition are per-rule enforcement, kept in core:verification rather than the profile, and the exact never-scanned trees remain deferred to the stack's single excluded-trees list (roots.excluded) as classified by the checker.
